root.name: Scotch Game: Braune Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Qh4 5. Be3

overview: In the Steinitz Scotch, 5.Be3 develops the bishop and leaves e4 unprotected, so Black can grab it with the queen. White then gets a lead in development and hits the black queen and the c6 knight. The line is rare and risky for White.

white_ideas.idea: Win time attacking the queen with Nb5/Bd3/Nc3

black_ideas.idea: Take e4 and bring the queen back to safety
Trade down and keep the extra pawn

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after the d-pawn trade
Exposed black queen against fast white pieces

character.notes: Forcing and tactical: an early queen raid and a pawn offer.

gambit.notes: The e4 pawn is unprotected and Black can keep it with an accurate queen retreat.

soundness.notes: Strong players think Black is doing well after taking the pawn.

structure.notes: Open lines for pieces after the centre pawns come off.

approach.notes: Rare, chosen mostly by club players for surprise.

level.notes: Some tactics have to be known but it is not a first repertoire choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Main 5.Nc3
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Qh4 5. Nc3
sublines_that_differ.how: the main line against the early queen sortie

character.reason: Queen sorties and a pawn offer make play forcing.

gambit.reason: White allows ...Qxe4 for a lead in development.

soundness.reason: Black seems fine after taking the pawn.

structure.reason: The centre pawns come off and pieces rule.

plans.reason: White gains time against the queen.
